study_identification_part.si_4_title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Six sites were used: (1) HCP Young Adult (n=1044), (2) HCP Development (n=201), (3) UK Biobank (n=5000), (4) Amsterdam Open MRI Collection Population Imaging of Psychology (AOMIC PIOP2; n=200; no matching dataset name in the list, classified as SINGLE-SITE), (5) Duke Neurogenetics Study (DNS; n=1246; no matching dataset name in the list, classified as SINGLE-SITE), and (6) MIND-Set (n=309 total: 37 reference + 36 clinical test controls + 236 patients). MIND-Set is mapped to the MIND-Set entry in the dataset list. Total reference sample N=7728.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We collated a large reference sample from 6 independent sites for whom high quality fMRI data for the EFMT are available: AOMIC PIOP2, Duke Neurogenetics Study, HCP Development, HCP Young Adult (1200 release), UK Biobank, and the MIND-Set cohort which also includes a clinical population."

answer.UK Biobank: normative reference (training and testing); additional out-of-sample validation (separate 5000 participants)

answer.MIND-Set: normative reference (37 controls for training/testing); clinical test application (236 patients)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: All six sites contributed to the reference normative model (N=7728). Data were split into stratified train/test halves (faces>shapes: train 3885, test 3843; faces>baseline: train 3778, test 3950). HCP Young Adult retest data (n=42) was used for test-retest reliability. An additional 5000 UK Biobank participants were used for supplementary out-of-sample validation. The MIND-Set patient cohort (n=236) was used as a clinical test sample to evaluate normative models.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "we split the data into training and test splits, stratified by site (face>shapes -train: 3885, test: 3843; faces>baseline -train: 3778, test: 3950)" ... "We tested the normative models we created using the reference data, with a heterogeneous patient sample from the MIND-Set cohort (n = 236)" ... "We collated a new sample of 5000 participants from UK Biobank to test against the reference models."
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Savage2024.pdf.md: Results / Fitting reference normative models, L45; Methods / Clinical application, L247; Methods / Supplementary out of sample test, L243

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Both models use the same total reference cohort of 7728 participants from 6 sites (HCP-YA: 1044, HCP-D: 201, UK Biobank: 5000, AOMIC PIOP2: 200, DNS: 1246, MIND-Set reference controls: 37). The data were split into train/test halves stratified by site. The faces>shapes model had train=3885, test=3843. The faces>baseline model had train=3778, test=3950. The difference in split sizes between models is because data availability differed slightly between contrasts.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "we estimated normative models of EFMT-related BOLD activation for the face>shapes and faces>baseline contrast using data from 7728 individuals across the lifespan. To achieve this, we split the data into training and test splits, stratified by site (face>shapes -train: 3885, test: 3843; faces>baseline -train: 3778, test: 3950)"
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.location: Savage2024.pdf.md: Results / Fitting reference normative models, L45

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics per site from Table 1: HCP-YA (n=1044): 28.76 ± 3.70 [22-37]; HCP-D (n=201): 13.86 ± 3.83 [8-21]; UK Biobank (n=5000): 63.94 ± 7.45 [46-82]; AOMIC PIOP2 (n=200): 22.16 ± 1.79 [18.25-26.25]; DNS (n=1246): 20.22 ± 1.21 [18.09-23.07]; MIND-Set reference (n=37): 38.0 ± 16.11 [20-74]. Weighted mean = sum(n_i * mean_i) / N_total = 49.63. Pooled SD computed accounting for within- and between-group variance = 20.59. Min inferred from HCP-D range (8). Max inferred from UK Biobank range (82). Both models share the same overall reference cohort, so overall-phase age statistics are the same. Train-phase age breakdowns are not reported.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Sex counts summed from Table 1 per site: HCP-YA 561F/483M, HCP-D 110F/91M, UK Biobank 2495F/2505M, AOMIC PIOP2 114F/86M, DNS 707F/539M, MIND-Set reference 21F/16M. Total female = 561+110+2495+114+707+21 = 4008 (51.9%). Total male = 483+91+2505+86+539+16 = 3720 (48.1%). Male counts were inferred by subtracting female N from site total N. Both models share the same overall reference cohort. Train-phase sex breakdowns are not reported.
